prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Choose Your New Desktop Pet", "Select a ready-to-go companion or build a custom pet using your own photos."]
1: ["Say Hello to Your Companion", "Click on your pet to see how it responds on your desktop screen."]
2: ["Bringing Your Pet to Life", "We are preparing your companion desktop graphics. This takes just a moment."]
3: ["Your Desktop Companion Awaits", "Explore how your pet lives on your desktop alongside your daily work."]
4: ["Sign in with your main account so your pet and progress stay saved across devices."]
5: ["You can minimize this window. We will notify you as soon as your pet is ready!"]
6: ["Pet not showing on screen? Click the system tray icon or press Alt+P to summon your pet."]
7: ["For best results, upload bright, well-lit photos of your pet facing directly toward the camera."]
8: ["Select Your Pet Setup Path", "Pick a ready companion or create a custom pet in just a few quick steps."]
9: ["Your Companion is Ready!", "Your companion is now active on your desktop screen.", "Interactive Care Unlocked"]
